findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
Observed the back storage room off the kitchen (water heater storage closet) to have bagged flour and boxed powdered foods to be stored in the unfinished space. The ceiling is not tiled and the floor is not coved. There is slight water seepage occurring around the floor. The room was previously observed with mouse droppings around the floor. Today, no droppings are observed, however, the space should have no food stored within or should have food protected if it is going to be used for food storage. Use large plastic storage tubs if you are going to continue to use the space for food storage. Provide storage bins that can be contained and are plastic or change the storage location of powdered foods.

Several food contact surfaces in the kitchen are thickly coated with accumulated dust and grease. The baffles of the hood system are coated in a layer of dust (baffles over the chicken broaster units). The broaster units themselves are observed to be coated with accumulated grease as is the surrounding floor and wall. See that the baffles are being routinely cleaned at a frequency that allows them to be maintained free of accumulated dust and grease.  After the baffles are clean, see that the baffles are cleaned a single one at a time and then moved down so that they maintain them clean. Clean the area surrounding the broaster (wall, floor, and attached plumbing).

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed raw chicken livers with no protective coverings to be stored above ready-to-eat pouches of cheese sauce. PIC was informed of proper storage order practices and the items were rearranged. Ensure staff are educated on proper storage order. Raw meat should never be stored above ready-to-eat foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Repeat Violation

The dish machine was observed to measure 0ppm chlorine during today’s inspection. The PIC was informed and trouble-shot the machine. The PIC discovered that the tubing was not placed deep enough into the sanitizer bucket to reach the liquid level. The tubing was adjusted and the machine was primed. The dish machine then measured 50ppm chlorine. PIC was informed to monitor the dish machine more frequently with test strips and ensure there are additional buckets of sanitizer available in the facility when the level in the bucket is low.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Observed the exterior door in the kitchen to have a damaged door seal. Incomplete door seals can promote the encroachment of pests in a facility. Ensure the seal is replaced by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.15(A) Outer Openings, Protected. (A) Except as specified in (B), (C), and (E) and under (D) of this section, outer openings of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against the entry of insects and rodents by: (1) Filling or closing holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings; (2) Closed, tight-fitting windows; and (3) Solid, self-closing, tight-fitting doors.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Observed a deceased mouse and mouse droppings in the back and front utility room in the kitchen. There are traps placed throughout the facility to control the presence of rodents in the facility. Inspector recommends increasing pest control action in the facility. A follow-up will be conducted on June 6th, 2025 to monitor cleaning of the droppings and increase of pest control in the facility.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: Upon arrival the inspector noted a mop bucket sitting in front of the kitchen’s only hand sink. The inspector asked for the mop bucket to be removed so that the hand sink could be accessed. Take care to never block the hand sink. The violation is considered corrected on site. Maintain access to the hand sink unobstructed.

(A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: Inspector observed the ice machine drop guard to be soiled with a pink substance. The food employee immediately prepared a chlorine sanitizer solution and cleaned and sanitized the drop guard. The violation is considered corrected on site. Ensure that the drop guard of the ice machine is checked regularly and maintained free of accumulated soil.

(E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: The inspector observed the dish machine chlorine supply bucket to be low and clear in color. The inspector tested the machine and found that there was not a testable level of chlorine. The facility manager changed out the bucket of sanitizer, primed and ran the machine. The machine is now testing at 50ppm of available chlorine as required by the machine specifications. The violation was corrected on site. Test machine daily to ensure that the sanitizer function of the machine is working properly.

Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: Soda dispensing nozzles of the soda machine are observed soiled with mold. The food employee removed all nozzles and immediately washed, rinsed and sanitized them. The violation is corrected on site. Maintain the soda nozzles free of accumulated mold and soil. 
 
(A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-202.15: Inspector observed the door behind the water heater in the kitchen to have a hole in the bottom where daylight is clearly visible. Repair or replace the door by the next routine inspection. 

(A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: Inspector observed a wet wiping cloth sitting on the pizza prep table. Store wet wiping cloths in sanitizer between uses. Develop a habit of putting wet wiping cloths back into sanitizer between uses for storage.

(A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-903.11: The facility has a box of napkins, a box of hot drink lids on the floor in the back storage room. This a repeat violation. Ensure that proper storage of single use items is taking place in the facility. 

(A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.
